:::{#exm-gaussian-exponential-family}
#### The Gaussian distribution with known variance is an exponential family

<!-- no-figure: the example checks an algebraic identity at the observed values -->

Let $\Rvar \sim \Normal(\mean, \varpar)$,
the [Gaussian distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-normal)
with [mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) $\mean \in \reals$
and a [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) $\varpar > 0$ that we treat as known.
Its [density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf) is
$\paren{2 \pi \varpar}^{-1/2} \expf{-\paren{\rvar - \mean}^2 / \paren{2 \varpar}}$.
We rewrite it in the form of @eq-exponential-family
by expanding the [square](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-square)
in the [exponent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-power-exponent)
and separating the factors that involve $\mean$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pdf\paren{\rvar ; \mean}
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \varpar}} \, \expf{-\frac{\paren{\rvar - \mean}^2}{2 \varpar}}
&& \text{(Gaussian density)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \varpar}} \, \expf{-\frac{\rvar^2 - 2 \rvar \mean + \mean^2}{2 \varpar}}
&& \text{(the square of a difference)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \varpar}} \, \expf{-\frac{\rvar^2}{2 \varpar} + \frac{\rvar \mean}{\varpar} - \frac{\mean^2}{2 \varpar}}
&& \text{(divide each term by the denominator)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \varpar}} \, \expf{-\frac{\rvar^2}{2 \varpar}} \, \expf{\frac{\mean}{\varpar} \rvar - \frac{\mean^2}{2 \varpar}}
&& \text{(the exponential of a sum is the product of the exponentials)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The [statistic](sufficiency.qmd#def-statistic) is $\statf{\rvar} = \rvar$,
and $\basemeasuref{\rvar} = \expf{-\rvar^2 / \paren{2 \varpar}} / \sqrt{2 \pi \varpar}$,
which does not involve $\mean$.
The [natural parameter](#def-natural-parameter) is $\natparam = \mean / \varpar$.
Inverting it gives $\mean = \varpar \natparam$,
so $\mean^2 / \paren{2 \varpar} = \varpar \natparam^2 / 2$.
Hence the Gaussian distributions with a known variance are an [exponential family](#def-exponential-family) with
$\logpartitionf{\natparam} = \varpar \natparam^2 / 2$.

To check the algebra on data,
we use the birth weights in grams from the `birthwt` data [@hosmer1989applied], <!-- check-term-links: allow: "weights" here is body weight, not the weights of a model -->
as distributed in R's `MASS` package [@venables2002modern].
We set $\mean$ to the [sample mean](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-mean)
and $\varpar$ to the [sample variance](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-variance) of the birth weights,
and evaluate both sides of @eq-exponential-family at every observed birth weight.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: gaussian-exponential-family-r
#| code-fold: false
bwt <- MASS::birthwt$bwt
mean_bwt <- mean(bwt)
sd_bwt <- sd(bwt)
variance <- sd_bwt^2

natural_parameter <- mean_bwt / variance
log_partition <- variance * natural_parameter^2 / 2

base_exponent <- -bwt^2 / (2 * variance)
base_scale <- sqrt(2 * pi * variance)
base_measure <- exp(base_exponent) / base_scale

exponent <- natural_parameter * bwt - log_partition
exponential_form <- base_measure * exp(exponent)
normal <- dnorm(bwt, mean = mean_bwt, sd = sd_bwt)

relative_difference <- abs(normal - exponential_form) / normal
max_relative_difference <- max(relative_difference)

tibble::tibble(bwt, normal, exponential_form)
max_relative_difference
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: gaussian-exponential-family-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import norm

birthwt = pd.read_csv("data/birthwt.csv")
bwt = birthwt["bwt"]
mean_bwt = bwt.mean()
variance = bwt.var(ddof=1)

natural_parameter = mean_bwt / variance
log_partition = variance * natural_parameter**2 / 2

base_measure = np.exp(-bwt**2 / (2 * variance)) / np.sqrt(2 * np.pi * variance)
exponential_form = base_measure * np.exp(natural_parameter * bwt - log_partition)
normal = norm.pdf(bwt, loc=mean_bwt, scale=np.sqrt(variance))

table = pd.DataFrame(
    {"bwt": bwt, "normal": normal, "exponential_form": exponential_form}
)
print(table.head())
print(np.max(np.abs(normal - exponential_form) / normal))
```

:::

For these data, $\natparam = `r signif(natural_parameter, 3)`$ per gram.
The two columns agree to within rounding error:
the largest relative difference is `r format(max_relative_difference, digits = 2)`.
:::
